SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Firms = {"f1", "f2"}
    EpochBound = 2
INVARIANT OrdersAreCredentialed
PROPERTY EveryOrderResolved
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction against a membership configuration that
is versioned by an epoch number. Each reconfiguration advances the epoch, and
every member firm's trading credential is stamped with the epoch it was issued
for, so a reconfiguration silently turns every outstanding credential stale. A
firm renews its credential for the live epoch only if it was carrying a
credential for the immediately preceding epoch - membership is meant to be
continuous - and each renewal is written into the exchange's admissions book for
that epoch. The exchange's market-operations officer holds a privileged override
and may grant a firm a credential for the live epoch with no continuity
requirement at all, which is how a firm that lapsed gets back in; such a grant is
written into the very same admissions book, so the override is privileged but
never invisible. A firm may put an order in at any time; the auction accepts the
order into that epoch's accepted-orders record only if the firm's credential is
stamped for the live epoch, and turns it away otherwise. The full action set is:
reconfigure into the next epoch, renew a credential under the continuity rule,
grant a credential by market-operations override, put in an order, accept an
order from a currently credentialed firm, and turn away an order from a firm
whose credential has gone stale.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every epoch, the firms recorded as having orders accepted in
that epoch are all listed in that epoch's admissions book, and no epoch beyond the
live one has any accepted orders at all, so no uncredentialed firm and no firm
acting on a stale credential ever gets an order into the auction.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every order that is put in is eventually resolved, either
accepted into the auction or turned away as stale.

---- MODULE W4Od10m0p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Blocks, VerBound

NoTrain == "notrain"
NoBlock == "noblock"

Claims == [t : Trains, b : Blocks, v : 0 .. (VerBound - 1)]

VARIABLES ver, holder, inBlock, grant, pool

vars == <<ver, holder, inBlock, grant, pool>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ ver \in [Blocks -> 0 .. (VerBound - 1)]
  /\ holder \in [Blocks -> Trains \cup {NoTrain}]
  /\ inBlock \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {NoBlock}]
  /\ grant \in [Trains -> Blocks \cup {NoBlock}]
  /\ pool \in SUBSET Claims

Init ==
  /\ ver = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
  /\ holder = [b \in Blocks |-> NoTrain]
  /\ inBlock = [t \in Trains |-> NoBlock]
  /\ grant = [t \in Trains |-> NoBlock]
  /\ pool = {}

Idle(t) == grant[t] = NoBlock /\ inBlock[t] = NoBlock

\* Optimistic read: the claim carries the version the train saw, nothing is held.
PostClaim(t, b) ==
  /\ Idle(t)
  /\ \A m \in pool : m.t # t
  /\ pool' = pool \cup {[t |-> t, b |-> b, v |-> ver[b]]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, holder, inBlock, grant>>

Matches(m) ==
  /\ ver[m.b] = m.v
  /\ ver[m.b] % 2 = 0
  /\ Idle(m.t)

\* The pool is a set, so claims are examined in whatever order the network likes.
GrantClaim(m) ==
  /\ m \in pool
  /\ Matches(m)
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![m.b] = (ver[m.b] + 1) % VerBound]
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![m.b] = m.t]
  /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![m.t] = m.b]
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED inBlock

DenyClaim(m) ==
  /\ m \in pool
  /\ ~Matches(m)
  /\ pool' = pool \ {m}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, holder, inBlock, grant>>

RollIn(t) ==
  /\ grant[t] # NoBlock
  /\ inBlock[t] = NoBlock
  /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = grant[t]]
  /\ grant' = [grant EXCEPT ![t] = NoBlock]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, holder, pool>>

\* Leaving flips the version back to even, which is what makes any claim taken
\* against the odd version fail on retry.
LeaveBlock(t) ==
  /\ inBlock[t] # NoBlock
  /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![inBlock[t]] = (ver[inBlock[t]] + 1) % VerBound]
  /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![inBlock[t]] = NoTrain]
  /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = NoBlock]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<grant, pool>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Trains : \E b \in Blocks : PostClaim(t, b)
  \/ \E m \in Claims : GrantClaim(m) \/ DenyClaim(m)
  \/ \E t \in Trains : RollIn(t) \/ LeaveBlock(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A train on the track is the recorded holder of the block it is in; since a
\* block records one holder, no two trains share a block.
OccupantIsHolder ==
  \A t \in Trains : inBlock[t] # NoBlock => holder[inBlock[t]] = t
====
nl:
A subway signalling system protects each track block with a version counter that
the interlocking keeps: an even version means the block is free, an odd version
means it is held, and the interlocking also records which train holds it. Trains
work optimistically instead of waiting on anything. A train reads a block's
version and posts a claim carrying that version into the signalling network. The
network does not preserve order - claims sit in an unordered pool and the
interlocking may pick up any waiting claim before any other, so a claim posted
earlier can easily be examined after one posted later. The interlocking grants a
claim only if the version it carries still matches the block's live version, that
version is even, and the claiming train is neither already granted a block nor
already inside one; granting advances the block's version to odd and records the
claimant as the holder. Any other claim is denied and the train simply reads
again and posts a new claim, which is the retry. A train with a grant rolls into
the block. Leaving the block advances the version back to even and clears the
recorded holder. The full action set is: read a block's version and post a claim,
grant a matching claim, deny a claim that no longer matches, roll into a granted
block, and leave a block.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A train is inside a track block only when the interlocking's
record names that same train as the holder of that block, and since a block has
exactly one recorded holder, two trains can never be inside the same block at
once.

---- MODULE W4Od7m8p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Bays, SlotsPerBay, PileHeight

Slots == Bays \X (1 .. SlotsPerBay)
BayOf(s) == s[1]

NoCrane == "nocrane"
NoSlot == <<"noslot", 0>>

VARIABLES coarse, fine, lifting, pile, failed

vars == <<coarse, fine, lifting, pile, failed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ coarse \in [Bays -> Cranes \cup {NoCrane}]
  /\ fine \in [Slots -> Cranes \cup {NoCrane}]
  /\ lifting \in [Cranes -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ pile \in [Slots -> 0 .. PileHeight]
  /\ failed \in SUBSET Cranes

Holds(c) == (\E b \in Bays : coarse[b] = c) \/ (\E s \in Slots : fine[s] = c)

Init ==
  /\ coarse = [b \in Bays |-> NoCrane]
  /\ fine = [s \in Slots |-> NoCrane]
  /\ lifting = [c \in Cranes |-> NoSlot]
  /\ pile = [s \in Slots |-> PileHeight]
  /\ failed = {}

\* Coarse rung: one bay per crane.
TakeBay(c, b) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ coarse[b] = NoCrane
  /\ \A y \in Bays : coarse[y] # c
  /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![b] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, lifting, pile, failed>>

\* Fine rung: only inside the bay the crane already holds.
TakeSlot(c, s) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ coarse[BayOf(s)] = c
  /\ fine[s] = NoCrane
  /\ \A u \in Slots : fine[u] # c
  /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![s] = c]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, lifting, pile, failed>>

BeginLift(c, s) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ fine[s] = c
  /\ coarse[BayOf(s)] = c
  /\ lifting[c] = NoSlot
  /\ pile[s] > 0
  /\ lifting' = [lifting EXCEPT ![c] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, pile, failed>>

FinishLift(c) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ lifting[c] # NoSlot
  /\ pile[lifting[c]] > 0
  /\ pile' = [pile EXCEPT ![lifting[c]] = pile[lifting[c]] - 1]
  /\ lifting' = [lifting EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, failed>>

Release(c) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ lifting[c] = NoSlot
  /\ Holds(c)
  /\ coarse' = [b \in Bays |-> IF coarse[b] = c THEN NoCrane ELSE coarse[b]]
  /\ fine' = [s \in Slots |-> IF fine[s] = c THEN NoCrane ELSE fine[s]]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lifting, pile, failed>>

\* Silent failure: the crane stops without letting go of anything.
Fail(c) ==
  /\ c \notin failed
  /\ failed' = failed \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, lifting, pile>>

\* Only the watchdog can strip a failed crane, and it strips the lift too.
Reclaim(c) ==
  /\ c \in failed
  /\ Holds(c)
  /\ coarse' = [b \in Bays |-> IF coarse[b] = c THEN NoCrane ELSE coarse[b]]
  /\ fine' = [s \in Slots |-> IF fine[s] = c THEN NoCrane ELSE fine[s]]
  /\ lifting' = [lifting EXCEPT ![c] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pile, failed>>

Restore(c) ==
  /\ c \in failed
  /\ ~Holds(c)
  /\ failed' = failed \ {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, lifting, pile>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : \E b \in Bays : TakeBay(c, b)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : \E s \in Slots : TakeSlot(c, s) \/ BeginLift(c, s)
  \/ \E c \in Cranes : FinishLift(c) \/ Release(c) \/ Fail(c) \/ Reclaim(c) \/ Restore(c)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A c \in Cranes : WF_vars(Reclaim(c))

\* A lifting crane owns both rungs for the slot it is on; each lock has one
\* holder, so no slot is ever worked by two cranes.
LiftingCraneOwnsBothRungs ==
  \A c \in Cranes :
    lifting[c] # NoSlot =>
      (fine[lifting[c]] = c /\ coarse[BayOf(lifting[c])] = c)

FailedLocksReclaimed ==
  \A c \in Cranes : (c \in failed /\ Holds(c)) ~> ~Holds(c)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {"c1", "c2", "c3"}
    Bays = {"y1", "y2"}
    SlotsPerBay = 2
    PileHeight = 2
INVARIANT LiftingCraneOwnsBothRungs
PROPERTY FailedLocksReclaimed
nl:
A container terminal works its yard with cranes that must climb a two-level lock
ladder before touching a stack. The coarse level is the bay: a crane takes the
bay lock for one bay at a time. The fine level is the individual stack slot
inside that bay, and a crane may only take a slot lock for a slot in the bay it
already holds. A crane is allowed to begin lifting at a slot - the critical
operation, since two machines over one stack would collide - only while it holds
both the slot's lock and the enclosing bay's lock. Completing a lift takes one
container off the slot's pile and stands the crane down from the slot; a crane
may also release its locks and step away entirely. Any crane can fail silently:
it stops dead, with no signal, while still holding whatever locks it had. The
yard watchdog is the only thing that can prise locks out of a dead crane's hands,
and it will only do so for a crane recorded as failed; a failed crane may not be
brought back into service until the watchdog has stripped it of every lock it was
holding. The full action set is: take a bay lock, take a slot lock inside a held
bay, begin a lift holding both locks, complete a lift, release held locks, fail a
crane silently, reclaim a failed crane's locks, and return a stripped crane to
service.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A crane is lifting at a slot only while the yard's lock records
name that same crane as the holder of that slot's lock and of the enclosing bay's
lock, and since each lock names a single holder, two cranes can never be lifting
at the same slot.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Locks left in the hands of a crane that has failed are always
eventually reclaimed by the watchdog, so a silent failure never wedges a bay or a
slot forever.

---- MODULE W4Od6m0p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Ctrls, Slots, VerBound

NoCtrl == "noctrl"
NoSlot == "noslot"
NoSnap == VerBound

VARIABLES record, held, stamp, snap, want

vars == <<record, held, stamp, snap, want>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ record \in [Slots -> Ctrls \cup {NoCtrl}]
  /\ held \in [Ctrls -> SUBSET Slots]
  /\ stamp \in [Slots -> 0 .. (VerBound - 1)]
  /\ snap \in [Ctrls -> (0 .. (VerBound - 1)) \cup {NoSnap}]
  /\ want \in [Ctrls -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]

Init ==
  /\ record = [s \in Slots |-> NoCtrl]
  /\ held = [k \in Ctrls |-> {}]
  /\ stamp = [s \in Slots |-> 0]
  /\ snap = [k \in Ctrls |-> NoSnap]
  /\ want = [k \in Ctrls |-> NoSlot]

\* Optimistic read: nothing is held, only the stamp is remembered.
Read(k, s) ==
  /\ snap[k] = NoSnap
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![k] = stamp[s]]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![k] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, held, stamp>>

TakeOK(k) ==
  /\ want[k] # NoSlot
  /\ snap[k] = stamp[want[k]]
  /\ record[want[k]] = NoCtrl

\* Record and the controller's own list are written in the same step.
Take(k) ==
  /\ TakeOK(k)
  /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![want[k]] = k]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![k] = held[k] \cup {want[k]}]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![want[k]] = (stamp[want[k]] + 1) % VerBound]
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![k] = NoSnap]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![k] = NoSlot]

Retry(k) ==
  /\ want[k] # NoSlot
  /\ ~TakeOK(k)
  /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![k] = NoSnap]
  /\ want' = [want EXCEPT ![k] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<record, held, stamp>>

GiveBack(k, s) ==
  /\ s \in held[k]
  /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![s] = NoCtrl]
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![k] = held[k] \ {s}]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![s] = (stamp[s] + 1) % VerBound]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, want>>

\* The supervisor's reclaim strikes the slot from the record and from whichever
\* controller's list carries it, together.
Reclaim(s) ==
  /\ record[s] # NoCtrl
  /\ record' = [record EXCEPT ![s] = NoCtrl]
  /\ held' = [k \in Ctrls |-> held[k] \ {s}]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![s] = (stamp[s] + 1) % VerBound]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, want>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Ctrls : \E s \in Slots : Read(k, s) \/ GiveBack(k, s)
  \/ \E k \in Ctrls : Take(k) \/ Retry(k)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Reclaim(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Each controller's list is exactly what the shared record says it owns; the
\* record is a function, so no slot can be allocated twice.
AllocationsAgree ==
  \A k \in Ctrls : held[k] = {s \in Slots : record[s] = k}
====
nl:
A skyscraper's elevator bank is driven by two independent dispatch controllers -
the express controller and the local controller - which share one pool of lobby
departure slots. The pool keeps an allocation record naming, for each slot, the
controller it is currently allocated to, and each slot also carries a stamp that
changes every time its allocation changes. The controllers never hold anything
while they think: a controller reads the stamp of the slot it wants, keeping that
reading as a snapshot, and then attempts to take the slot. The attempt succeeds
only if the slot's stamp still equals the snapshot and the allocation record
still shows the slot free; a successful attempt writes the controller into the
allocation record, adds the slot to that controller's own list of slots it holds,
and changes the stamp so the other controller's snapshot of that slot is now
worthless. If the stamp has moved on or the slot has been taken in the meantime,
the controller throws its attempt away and reads again, which is the retry.
A controller can give a slot back, which clears the allocation record for that
slot, strikes it from that controller's list and changes the stamp. The building
supervisor can also reclaim a slot outright, and a reclaim likewise clears the
record, strikes the slot from whichever controller's list holds it, and changes
the stamp - record and lists always move together. The full action set is: read a
slot's stamp and target it, take a targeted slot, retry after a failed attempt,
give a held slot back, and reclaim a slot.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Each controller's list of slots it holds is exactly the set of
slots the pool's allocation record assigns to that controller, and since the
record assigns each slot to at most one controller, no slot is ever allocated to
both controllers at once.
